Privacy.dns_note: While protection is on, your phone looks up the addresses of sites it doesn't block through a public DNS service — Cloudflare or Quad9 — instead of your operator's. Like any DNS service, it sees the site's name and your connection's IP address. Cleanway does not receive these lookups.

items.q: To check a site we send only its name — never the full link, the page, or your messages. Everything we do receive is spelled out in our privacy policy.
We measure our phishing detection with an open script anyone can re-run, and we show a number only when the sample is big enough to mean something. Measured, not marketed.
Blocking scam sites is free and will stay free. Protection itself is never behind a paywall.
What does Cleanway learn about me?
items.a: Sites are checked against the list right on your phone. When a site needs a closer look, only its name (like example.com) goes to our server, which may ask services such as Google Safe Browsing about that name. We don't receive full links, page contents or message texts, and we don't keep a record of which sites you open. The details are in our privacy policy.

items.q: Will it slow my phone down?
items.a: The list check runs on the phone itself and takes a fraction of a second. Cleanway looks only at the names of the sites your phone connects to, not at what you do on them.

items.q: Can I use it together with a VPN?
items.a: Not at the same time. Cleanway's protection uses Android's VPN mechanism only for site names: the phone checks each name against the list and looks up the ones that aren't blocked in a public DNS service (Cloudflare or Quad9). The rest of your traffic goes as usual — not through Cleanway and not through another country. Android runs only one such service at a time, so if you turn on another VPN, Cleanway's protection switches off. When you are done, open Cleanway and turn protection back on. Checking a site or a message by hand in the app keeps working either way.

items.q: How is this different from Google Safe Browsing?
items.a: Google Safe Browsing is one of the sources we use. Cleanway also blocks known scam sites in every app on the phone, not only in the browser, checks suspicious messages on the phone, and explains its verdicts in plain words. When we ask Google about a site, we send only its name — not who you are.
Yes. Blocking scam sites is free and works without an account. Where paid extras are offered, they never switch the protection itself off.

No, and nobody can honestly promise that. Cleanway blocks sites that are already on the list of known scam sites. Links you open through Cleanway are also checked in the background, but a warning, if any, comes after the page has opened, and a brand-new scam site can open with no warning at all. Never enter card details or codes from text messages on a site you opened from a message link.

items.q: Will Cleanway ever call me or text me a link?
items.a: No. Cleanway never calls and never sends links by text message. If someone calls or writes in Cleanway's name and asks you to install something, read out a code or switch protection off, it is a scam.

Dns.page_title: Phishing-blocking DNS — one tap, no app
Dns.page_description: Install the Cleanway DNS filter in 30 seconds on iPhone, Mac or Windows. System-wide protection — no VPN, no app. On Android, use the free Cleanway app.
Dns.hero_title: Block phishing on every app — without installing one
Dns.hero_subtitle: Cleanway runs a phishing-blocking DNS resolver. Point your phone or laptop at it and every app on the device — Safari, Chrome, Mail, banking apps — gets the same protection.
Dns.hero_meta: Works on iOS 14+, iPadOS 14+, macOS 11+ and Windows 11. No VPN. Won’t drain your battery. On Android — the free Cleanway app.
Dns.ios_intro: Tap the button below on your iPhone or iPad. iOS will ask permission to install a configuration profile.
Dns.ios_step1: Tap “Allow” when iOS asks to download the profile.
Dns.ios_step2: Open Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → Cleanway DNS.
Dns.ios_step3: Tap “Install” twice, then enter your device passcode.
Dns.ios_unsigned_note: If iOS shows “Unsigned”, that’s expected — Apple’s signing program is paid and we’d rather not pass the cost on to you. The profile itself is unchanged whether it’s signed or not.
Dns.android_app_intro: On Android, protection comes with the free Cleanway app: it blocks scam sites in every app and tells you right away.
Dns.android_undo_body: Please switch it back: open “Private DNS” in Settings (on Samsung: Connections → More connection settings) and choose “Automatic”. This setup isn’t supported yet, and with it your phone may lose internet.
Dns.win_intro: Windows 11 supports DNS-over-HTTPS natively. Earlier Windows versions need a third-party tool like Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 — sorry.
Dns.win_step1: Open Settings → Network & internet → Wi-Fi → click your network → DNS server assignment → Edit.
Dns.win_step2: Switch to Manual, turn on IPv4, set preferred DNS to 1.1.1.1 with DNS over HTTPS “On (manual template)”.
Dns.benefits_heading: What does this protect me from?
Dns.benefit_1: Phishing links in SMS, email, and Telegram open as a “site not found” instead of a credential-stealing page.
Dns.benefit_2: Known malware command-and-control hosts are stopped before your phone can reach them — as long as they are on the list.
Dns.benefit_3: Brand-impersonation domains (paypal-secure-login.com) are blocked at the resolver level — your browser never even loads them.
Dns.benefit_4: Works on every app, not just your browser. WhatsApp links, banking apps, in-app browsers — all protected.
Dns.privacy_heading: Privacy — what we see and what we don’t
Dns.privacy_body: Cleanway DNS resolves the domain only. We never log the queries to disk, never send them to Sentry, never sell them to anyone. Queries stay in memory just long enough to answer the request.
Dns.privacy_logs: What we DO keep: an anonymous daily counter of total queries and total blocks, used to publish our quarterly transparency report. No domains, no IPs, no users.
Dns.layer_heading: Where DNS fits in your protection
Dns.layer_body: DNS is the widest layer — it protects every app on your device, not just the browser. It is also the shallowest: it can only block a domain that is already on our phishing blocklist. It cannot read a page, so on its own it will not catch a brand-new phishing kit the moment it appears, or a credential form hiding on a trusted-but-hacked site.
Dns.layer_extension: For that deeper protection, add the Cleanway browser extension. It runs the full per-page analysis on every site you open, spots look-alike login forms in real time, and warns you before you type a password. DNS covers the widest surface; the extension adds the deepest checks — together they cover both.
Dns.layer_generic: This is not a generic DNS filter. Cleanway DNS is tuned specifically for phishing and credential theft, driven by the same threat intelligence that powers the extension — not a repurposed ad-blocking list.

Methodology.page_description: How Cleanway measures its own phishing detection: the datasets, the script, and when a number is allowed on the site.
Methodology.hero_title: How we measure our own detection rate
Methodology.hero_subtitle: Every accuracy number we show points here: the data, the script, and how to re-run it yourself.
Methodology.why_p1: A detection rate is only worth something if you can see how it was measured. So we publish the script, the data sources and every weekly result.
Methodology.why_p2: The script runs every Monday against fresh phishing links from public feeds and a sample of legitimate sites. Results are committed to our public GitHub repository — including the weeks when the numbers look bad.
Methodology.results_unavailable: No benchmark snapshot is available right now.
Methodology.verdict_mapping_heading: How each service's answer is counted
Methodology.verdict_mapping_p1: Services answer in different ways. We reduce every answer to dangerous, safe or unknown. Unknown answers (rate-limited, not indexed, error) are counted separately — neither right nor wrong.
Methodology.reproduce_p1: You need git and Python 3. The script downloads the same feeds, runs the same comparisons and writes the same JSON:
Methodology.cadence_p1: The benchmark runs every Monday at 05:15 UTC in GitHub Actions and commits its results to docs/benchmarks/. If recall drops by more than 5 percentage points from the previous week, the workflow opens a pull request that flags it.
Methodology.results_not_publishable: The latest snapshot ({date}) is too small to quote: {phishing} phishing links, {classified} of them with a Cleanway verdict. We show numbers only when a run has at least {min_phishing} phishing links and at least {min_classified} verdicts. Every weekly run, small ones included, is in the repository.
Methodology.results_snapshot: Snapshot: {date}. Sample: {phishing} phishing links, {legit} legitimate sites.
Methodology.fp_not_measured: We show no false-alarm rate for this run: too few real sites got an answer from Cleanway, or the sample holds only sites our server treats as safe without checking (see the caveats below).
Methodology.dataset_phishing_desc: fresh links from the URLhaus and PhishTank public feeds, downloaded at each run and de-duplicated by domain.
Methodology.dataset_safe_desc: random domains from the Tranco top-1M list, ranks 100 to 100,000, with a fixed random seed so the sample can be reproduced.
Methodology.dataset_safe_desc_curated: real Russian sites outside the Tranco top 100,000 — regional and city administrations, universities, .рф sites, small banks and businesses, museums and theatres — from a published list that gives the source of every site, sampled with a fixed random seed.
Methodology.mapping_cleanway: Cleanway: "dangerous" counts as dangerous, "safe" as safe, "caution" as unknown.
Methodology.mapping_cloudflare: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 for Families: a blocked answer (NXDOMAIN or 0.0.0.0 / ::) counts as dangerous, a normal answer as safe.
Methodology.mapping_virustotal: VirusTotal: dangerous when at least 2 of its vendors flag the link; a single vendor is ignored as too noisy.
Methodology.caveat_endpoint: Cleanway is measured through its public site-check endpoint — the same anonymous path a visitor uses — not through a privileged one. It measures our server's verdict, not blocking on the phone: the phone's protection blocks straight away only the sites on its list, so this number does not say how many of these links a phone would block.
Methodology.caveat_rate_limit: Right now the weekly run is slowed down by that endpoint's rate limit, so many links get no verdict and most runs are too small to publish.
Methodology.caveat_phishtank: PhishTank's free lookup often answers "not indexed" for fresh links because its database lags by a few hours, so its column often shows "—".
Methodology.caveat_gsb: Google Safe Browsing needs an API key; when none is configured for the run, its column shows "—".
Methodology.caveat_nxdomain: A domain that no longer exists also gets NXDOMAIN from Cloudflare and is counted as a Cloudflare block, which flatters Cloudflare on phishing domains that have already been taken down.
Methodology.caveat_latency: Response times are measured from the machine that runs the script (a cloud runner in the US or EU); from other regions they will differ.
Methodology.caveat_allowlist: Our server treats sites in the Tranco top 100,000 as safe without analysing them, and the sample of real sites above comes from that same range. So it cannot show how often Cleanway wrongly calls a less famous real site dangerous, and we publish no false-alarm rate from it. We will once the sample includes real sites outside that list.
Methodology.caveat_allowlist_curated: Our server treats sites in the Tranco top 100,000 as safe without analysing them, so the sample of real sites above is taken from outside that list: every one of them is really analysed. Our server is outside Russia, and some of these sites do not answer foreign visitors; the weekly results on GitHub show the false alarms on those sites separately.

Support.title: Support
Support.subtitle: Answers to common questions, and what to do if something goes wrong.
Support.email_hint: Please include your phone model and what happened.
Support.q_vpn: Is this a VPN that hides my traffic?
Support.a_vpn: No. Cleanway uses Android's VPN mechanism only to run a local filter on your phone that blocks scam sites in every app. It does not hide where you go and does not send your traffic through another country. To reach the sites it doesn't block, your phone looks up their names, as it would without Cleanway, with your mobile operator's or Wi-Fi router's DNS server — and only if that doesn't answer, with Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Quad9 (9.9.9.9).
Support.a_install: Download the app, open the file and allow the installation — the Android page walks through every warning you may see on the way. On the first run, tap "Turn on protection" and allow the connection Android asks about.
Support.q_off: How do I turn it off?
Support.a_off: Open the app and tap "Pause protection". You can turn it back on anytime.
Support.q_fp: A safe site is blocked — what do I do?
Support.a_fp: Open Cleanway, go to the History tab and tap that site. Then tap "Not a scam — allow it" and confirm. Cleanway will stop blocking the site on your phone. If someone on the phone is asking you to allow a site, it's a scammer. Hang up. Allow a site only if you are sure it is the real one.
Support.a_privacy: Sites are checked against the list on your phone. When a site needs a closer look, only its name goes to our server — not the full link and not who you are. The text of messages you check never leaves the phone. The full details are in the privacy policy.
Support.email_not_live_body: Our support mailbox is still being set up, so messages to support@cleanway.ai may not reach us. Please don't send anything important there for now. The answers below cover the most common problems.
Support.q_app_vpn: Another app asks me to turn off my VPN
Support.a_app_vpn: Some apps — banks, messengers, government services — refuse to work while any VPN is on, and to Android, Cleanway's protection looks like one. Open Cleanway, tap "Pause protection", use that app, then turn protection back on.
Support.q_no_internet: The internet stopped working after I installed Cleanway
Support.a_no_internet: First pause protection in Cleanway and check whether sites open. If you ever typed dns.cleanway.ai into "Private DNS" in your phone's settings, set it back to "Automatic" — that setting stops Cleanway from working and can cut off the internet.
Support.a_calls: Cleanway never calls and never sends links by text message. If someone calls or writes in Cleanway's name and asks you to install something, read out a code or switch protection off — hang up. It is a scam.

sections.title: 1. What Cleanway is
paragraphs: Cleanway helps protect you from scam and phishing sites. It consists of the Android app, the site check on cleanway.ai and a DNS filter for iPhone, Mac and Windows. Cleanway checks site names against lists of known threats and other signals and tells you what it found.

sections.title: 2. What we do not promise
paragraphs: Cleanway's verdicts are advice, not a guarantee. We cannot promise that:
items: every scam or phishing site will be caught — new ones appear every day;
a safe site will never be flagged by mistake;
a brand-new scam site will be blocked the moment it appears;
Cleanway protects against every kind of fraud — for example, it does not protect against phone calls.
after: Use Cleanway as one layer of protection: never share codes from text messages, and check anything urgent by calling your bank on the number printed on your card.

sections.title: 3. Free use and accounts
paragraphs: Blocking scam sites is free and works without an account. An account is needed only for family features and paid plans. If you create one, use a real email address and keep access to it: you sign in with one-time codes or links sent there.

sections.title: 4. Paid plans
paragraphs: In some countries Cleanway offers paid plans with extras. Paid plans are not offered in Russia. Where they are offered, payment is handled by Stripe, the price and billing period are shown before you pay, and you can cancel at any time — the plan stays active until the end of the paid period. Refunds are handled as the law requires. Blocking scam sites never becomes a paid feature.

sections.title: 5. Acceptable use
paragraphs: Please don't:
items: use Cleanway to test or improve scam sites;
send automated bulk requests or try to get around request limits;
resell access to Cleanway's checks;
interfere with the service or attack its infrastructure;
use family features to harass or pressure anyone, or add a person to a family group without their consent.
after: We may limit or close access for anyone who does.

sections.title: 6. Family features
paragraphs: Family alerts are end-to-end encrypted: we cannot read them, and we cannot recover them if every device in the family loses its keys. A family alert is a helpful heads-up, not a replacement for talking to each other.

sections.title: 7. Privacy
paragraphs: How we handle data is described in the privacy policy.

sections.title: 8. Source code
paragraphs: Cleanway's source code is published on GitHub under the MIT licence.

sections.title: 9. Liability
paragraphs: Cleanway is provided "as is". To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect losses, and our total liability is limited to what you paid us in the last 12 months. Nothing in these terms limits rights that the law does not allow to be limited.

sections.title: 10. Changes
paragraphs: We may update these terms. We will publish important changes on this page before they take effect; the date at the top shows the current version.

section.title: 4. Subscription and payment
paragraphs: In Russia Cleanway is a subscription billed to your mobile phone account through your mobile operator and a payment aggregator. The plan's price and the charge date are shown before you confirm; the subscription starts only after you confirm it with an SMS code from your number. The first days after installation are a trial with nothing charged; its length and the prices are on the Pricing page.

The subscription renews every month until you cancel. You can cancel in the app, by SMS or through support — after cancelling nothing more is charged, and protection runs until the end of the paid month. We never charge an account into the negative and never create a debt. If protection did not work through our fault, or a charge went through after cancellation, we refund that month; this does not limit your statutory rights.

Prices can change for new subscriptions only: a running subscription keeps the price it was started at. In other countries paid plans are paid by bank card through Stripe — there too the price and period are shown before you pay, and you can cancel at any time.

billing.lapse_basic: If a payment still fails after the retries, the subscription is paused, but basic blocking of known scam sites keeps working at no charge — the list is refreshed once a week.
billing.lapse_off: If a payment still fails after the retries, the subscription is paused and protection switches off until the next payment.

PrivacyPolicy.meta_description: What Cleanway receives, what stays on your phone, who else sees what, and how long anything is kept.
PrivacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
PrivacyPolicy.intro: This policy explains in plain words what data Cleanway handles, why, and who else sees it. It describes the service as it works today. If something here does not match what Cleanway actually does, that is a mistake and we want to hear about it.
PrivacyPolicy.contact_live: Questions and requests about your data:
PrivacyPolicy.contact_not_live: Our support mailbox is still being set up, so we cannot receive email yet. This section will show the address as soon as it works.

sections.title: 1. In short
items: To check a site we need only its name (for example, example.com). We don't receive full links, page contents or the texts of your messages.
Most checks happen on your phone, against a list of known scam sites.
When a site needs a closer look, its name goes to our server, which may ask other checking services about that name — never about you.
You don't need an account to be protected. We don't show ads and don't sell data.

sections.title: 2. Who we are
paragraphs: Cleanway (cleanway.ai) protects against scam and phishing sites. It consists of an Android app, a site check on cleanway.ai and a DNS filter for iPhone, Mac and Windows. How to contact us is at the end of this policy.

sections.title: 3. The Android app: protection in every app
paragraphs: When you turn on protection, Cleanway starts a local filter using Android's VPN mechanism. Only DNS queries pass through it — the questions your phone asks to find a site's address, such as "where is example.com?". The contents of pages, your messages and calls do not go through the filter and are not read.

Each site name is compared with the list of scam sites stored on the phone. If it is on the list, the phone doesn't open the site, and a note (the site's name, the time and what happened) is saved on the phone for the app's History.

Names that are not on the list are passed on to find the site's address: first to the DNS server of the network the phone is on — your mobile operator's or your Wi-Fi router's — as without Cleanway. Only if it does not answer do they go to Cloudflare (1.1.1.1), then Quad9 (9.9.9.9), and as a last resort Cloudflare's encrypted DNS-over-HTTPS. This is how app versions 1.0.2 and 1.0.3 work; version 1.0.1 asked Cloudflare first. These services see the site name and your connection's IP address, as any DNS service does; their own privacy policies apply. Cleanway does not receive or store these queries.
From version 1.0.2 the app carries a copy of the scam-site list, used only until the phone downloads a fresh one.

sections.title: 4. The list of scam sites
paragraphs: The app downloads the list from our server (api.cleanway.ai) and refreshes it about every 6 hours, less often on mobile data. The request says nothing about the sites you visit: it carries only the usual technical details of any internet request, such as your IP address, and a marker of the list version the phone already has. From time to time the app also asks our server whether a newer version of the app is available.

sections.title: 5. Checking sites and links
paragraphs: A site's name — without the rest of the link, without page contents and without your account details — goes to our server when you check a site by hand (in the app or on cleanway.ai/check), and when you open a link through Cleanway that isn't on the list (from version 1.0.2 also when the “Every app” protection is off).
To decide whether the site is dangerous, our server may:
items: ask external checking services about the name: Google Safe Browsing, PhishTank, URLhaus, MalwareBazaar, ThreatFox, PhishStats, Spamhaus DBL, SURBL, AlienVault OTX and IPQualityScore, and look up when the site was registered through the RDAP service rdap.org. They receive only the site name, not who you are;
compare its answer with Cloudflare's DNS filter (1.1.1.1 for Families), which receives the site name in an ordinary DNS query;
look at the site itself (its address, certificate and settings) — from our server, not from your phone;
in borderline cases, ask an AI model made by Anthropic for a second opinion. It receives only abstract signals, without the site name.
after: The result is kept in our server's cache for up to 24 hours so that a repeat check is fast. It is tied to the site, not to you.

Your IP address is used to limit how many checks one connection can make. For that it is kept as is, as a counter in our server's memory, for up to an hour, and then deleted. The security log of account actions stores only a shortened cryptographic hash of it, never the address itself.

From version 1.0.2, the app also sends an install number with every check: a random number made on the phone and replaced with a new one every 24 hours. It is not tied to the phone, the SIM card or an account; it lets us limit checks per phone rather than for all the subscribers who share a carrier's IP address. Our server keeps only a cryptographic hash of it, as a counter, for up to an hour.

sections.title: 6. Checking messages
paragraphs: Cleanway does not read your text messages by itself and does not ask for access to them. It checks only a message you share with it or paste in.

The text is analysed on the phone and is not sent anywhere — not to us and not to anyone else. Up to three site names from links in the message may be checked on our server as described above, without the rest of the link. History keeps the verdict and the site names, never the text.

sections.title: 7. What stays on your phone
items: the list of scam sites;
check history — site names, verdicts, reasons and times — until you clear it in Settings;
the log of what protection blocked or warned about — the latest 200 events;
sites you allowed with "Not a scam";
keys for encrypted family alerts, in the phone's protected storage.

sections.title: 8. Account and email
paragraphs: An account is optional: it is needed only for family features and paid plans. If you create one, we store your email address, your plan, a random device ID (not derived from your phone's hardware) and your app settings. You sign in with a one-time code (in the app) or a one-time link (on the website) sent to your email; there is no password.
Accounts are stored with our database provider, Supabase. Supabase may also record the IP address a sign-in came from in its own security log.

sections.title: 9. Family
paragraphs: Family alerts are encrypted on the sender's device and can be read only on the recipients' devices. Our server stores only the encrypted text and cannot read it, but it does see who belongs to which family and who sent an alert to whom, and when. Alerts are kept for up to 30 days. Invitation codes and PINs are stored only as hashes.

sections.title: 10. The website and the DNS filter
paragraphs: cleanway.ai has no advertising or analytics trackers. Our hosting providers — Vercel for the website, Railway for the server — keep standard technical request logs, which can include the requested address and your IP address.

If you set up the Cleanway DNS filter (dns.cleanway.ai) on an iPhone, Mac or Windows computer, all of your device's DNS queries go to our server. It blocks names from the list and passes the rest to Cloudflare to find the address. Queries are not written to disk; for a blocked name, our log keeps at most its last 32 characters, without your IP address.

sections.title: 11. Error reports
paragraphs: The app, the website and our server may send Sentry technical error reports, so that we can fix bugs, and timing measurements for about one request in ten. We remove email addresses, IP addresses and access keys from error reports. A report or a measurement can still contain the address of a page or request — for example, the name of a site that was being checked. The website does not record sessions. Sentry keeps this data for up to 90 days.

sections.title: 12. Payments
paragraphs: Paid plans are not offered in Russia. Where they are offered, payment goes through Stripe: Stripe receives your email and the chosen plan and handles the card itself. We never see or store card details.

sections.title: 13. Who processes data for us
items: Railway — runs our server (api.cleanway.ai);
Vercel — hosts the website;
Supabase — stores accounts and family data;
GitHub — hosts the app file you download and sees your IP address when you download it;
Cloudflare and Quad9 — public DNS used by the app, see section 3;
the checking services listed in section 5, and Anthropic — receive site names or abstract signals only;
Sentry — error reports and timing measurements; Stripe — payments outside Russia.
after: These companies are based outside Russia, mainly in the USA and the EU, so the data they process is transferred abroad.

sections.title: 14. How long we keep data
items: site check results in the server cache — up to 24 hours;
your IP address in the check-limit counter — up to an hour;
account data — until you delete the account; after a deletion request we keep it for 30 more days in case you change your mind, then delete it;
the security log of account actions (with hashed IP addresses) — 2 years;
weekly counters for accounts (numbers only, no site names) — 1 year;
encrypted family alerts — up to 30 days;
data on your phone — until you clear it or remove the app.

sections.title: 15. Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask what data about you we hold, ask us to correct or delete it, and withdraw your consent. Without an account we don't know who you are: we have no name, email or phone number of yours — only the technical data described above, such as your IP address in the check counter and in hosting logs. To delete an account or make a request, contact us as described below. Removing the app deletes everything it stored on the phone.

sections.title: 16. Children
paragraphs: Cleanway is not meant for children under 13 to use on their own; family features are managed by an adult.

sections.title: 17. Changes and contact
paragraphs: If we change this policy, we will publish the new version on this page with a new date.

section.title: 12. Paying for the subscription
paragraphs: In Russia the subscription is billed to a mobile phone account. To set it up you enter a phone number — your own, or that of the relative who pays. The trial needs no number.

The phone number, the plan, the dates and the history of charges are kept in a separate database located in Russia, apart from the rest of Cleanway's data. The number is stored encrypted; in logs, error reports and on screens it is shown only in part. We hold no bank-card data: no card is involved in this payment.

Your mobile operator and the payment aggregator that process the charge receive the number and the amount — they handle that data under their own rules. We also keep a record of consent: which text and which price you saw and how you confirmed.

Payment and consent records are kept as long as accounting and tax rules require — up to five years; once the subscription is over and that period has passed, the phone number is deleted from the database. In other countries payment goes through Stripe: Stripe receives your email and the chosen plan and handles the card itself; we never see or store card details.
